name: Atmospheric CO₂
summary: CO₂ 428.5 ppm at Mauna Loa, up 3.31 ppm on a year, above the 3 ppm Alert line
state: Mauna Loa recorded 428.5 ppm in the week of 1 Nov, 3.31 ppm higher than a year earlier, above the 3 ppm/yr Alert line and up from 2.12 ppm on the previous weekly reading (NOAA GML). Weekly growth figures are noisy, but strong El Niño years usually speed up CO₂ growth as land carbon sinks weaken, and the ONI stands at +2.5 (NOAA CPC).
for_you: Faster CO₂ growth adds to long-term warming; it has no immediate effect on daily life.
rubric_hit: CO₂ y/y +3.31 ppm > 3.0 ppm Alert line

sources.title: NOAA GML — Trends in atmospheric CO₂ (Mauna Loa)

why: CO₂ concentration is the main long-run driver of warming; the growth rate shows whether emissions cuts are biting.
drivers: Fossil emissions, land sinks, El Niño (weakens sinks), wildfires.
